{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ee82bb40feb4e92460c34d65cb281192520f3bcec98c3a415856d8b82b14ab7a","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:29","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Preparing to drive and driver factors","heading":"C — Preparing to drive and driver factors","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Preparing to drive and driver factors

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Before driving, check that the tires have sufficient tread and the correct air pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Use the tire-pressure value in the owner's manual or driver-side door jamb and check it with a pressure gauge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, before driving or at least three hours after driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
If measured pressure is above the specified value, release air until it matches; if below, add air or seek tire-professional help. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Inspect tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long road trip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
For the penny tread check, hold Lincoln's body and insert his head into a groove where the tread appears lowest. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's head indicates the stated safe amount of tread. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
Tread below the penny-test level greatly reduces tire grip in adverse conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
Keep tire-changing equipment in the vehicle, including a spare, lug wrench, jack, flashlight, warning devices, wheel wedges, repair kit and gloves. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Check oil, washer fluid and fuel, and refill as the owner's manual directs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
Set the driver's seat so the pedals and controls are easy to reach and the windshield view is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A01
Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt on every trip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A01
Loose objects can become projectiles in a crash while continuing at the vehicle's pre-impact speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A01
Put heavy objects in the trunk when possible, or secure them with seat belts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A01
Do not place stored objects on the rear window deck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A01
Adjust the seat before setting the mirrors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A01
Set the rearview mirror to show traffic directly behind the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A01
Set side mirrors so the vehicle's side is barely visible when leaning toward that side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A01
Mirror settings may need to differ between drivers to remove blind spots. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A01
Do not hang objects from the rearview mirror while the vehicle is moving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A01
Tags, permits and placards may hang from the rearview mirror only while the vehicle is parked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A01
Nothing may be attached to the windshield where it obstructs the driver's road view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A02
Maintain fresh air in the vehicle to support alertness and guard against exhaust-related carbon monoxide poisoning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A02
Set the head restraint so its top reaches at least the height of the top of the driver's ears. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A02
A properly positioned head restraint can prevent or reduce neck-injury severity in a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A02
Always use prescription glasses or contacts while driving if you normally wear corrective lenses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A02
Do not use sunglasses or tinted contact lenses for night driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A02
Locking the doors and wearing a seat belt help prevent being thrown out during a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A02
Locked doors also reduce the likelihood of victimization when stopped at an intersection or parking area. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A02
A driving distraction takes attention from driving, eyes from the road or hands from the wheel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A02
Eating, drinking or smoking can draw hands and eyes away from driving and slow the response to hazards. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A02
Adjusting audio equipment is a driving distraction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A02
Headphones or earpieces may be used in only one ear and only for communication. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A02
A phone conversation can distract a driver even when the phone is hands-free. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A02
Interacting with passengers can distract the driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A02
Searching for or moving an item inside the vehicle is a distraction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A02
Reading, writing, texting and personal grooming can divert attention from driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A02
Staring at a crash, work zone or an off-road event can distract a driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A02
Tiredness slows reactions and impairs judgment and vision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: a blood alcohol level below a legal threshold does not make driving safe; hands-free calls can still distract; coffee and cold showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration.
Mnemonics: check the vehicle, fit the driver and keep attention on driving.
Glossary: a cold tire has not been driven recently; peripheral vision is side vision; a distraction diverts attention, eyes or hands from driving.
